        - heading "Understand ANOVA" [level=2]
        - paragraph: ANOVA tests whether several population means are equal by comparing between-group and within-group variation. You can learn ANOVA by trying one small example instead of long theory.
        - paragraph: State group mean hypotheses, compute an F statistic, and use the F distribution for the p-value. Try the example below. Write your steps and choose an answer before opening the comparison.
        - paragraph: "In real life, three teaching methods: Compare mean scores across groups. Watch out: Doing many pairwise tests instead of one overall ANOVA first. Use ANOVA for an overall comparison of several means."
